text:
A little boy watched his grandmother write a letter. “Grandma, are you writing about me?” he asked.

“Yes,” she said. “But I’m thinking about this pencil. I want you to be like it.”

The boy looked at the pencil. “Why? It looks like a normal pencil.”

“It has five important lessons,” she said. “First, you can do great things, but you need a hand to guide you. That hand is God, or the people who love you.

“Second, sometimes the pencil must be sharpened. It hurts a little, but it becomes better. Difficult times make you stronger.

“Third, the pencil has an eraser. You can fix your mistakes.

“Fourth, the most important part is inside, not outside.

“Fifth, the pencil always leaves a mark. Everything you do leaves a mark too. Be careful what you do.”

The boy smiled. He looked at the pencil again. “Now I understand,” he said.

Moral: Learn from every difficulty, and leave good marks on the world.
